summary.en: Choose a way to store data by the operations your program needs.
summary.bn: তোমার প্রোগ্রামে কী কাজ করতে হবে, তা দেখে ডেটা রাখার উপায় বেছে নাও।

notes: These implementations use C17. Compound literals and declarations in loop headers date from C99; C17 does not add automatic memory management.

examples.title: One marks collection, three operations
examples.explanationHtml: Index 2 selects the third mark. Updating one slot leaves the order unchanged; totaling visits all four slots.

examples.title: A bounded collection behind an interface
examples.explanationHtml: The interface reports success twice and failure once. Capacity is an implementation choice; failure must not overwrite a mark.

examples.title: A sequence whose links hold its order
examples.explanationHtml: The printed sequence follows next links. Separate allocations need not be adjacent, so the links carry the order.

practice.title: Read a mark by position
practice.statementHtml: Read n (1..16), n marks (-99..99), and index i (0..n-1). After the prompt, print Mark: followed by the selected mark.
hints: The first mark has index zero.

practice.title: Count a chosen value
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), n values (-99..99), then a target. Print Matches: and its occurrence count.
hints: Visit each slot because duplicates may appear.

practice.title: Preserve order while selecting passes
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n marks (0..99). Print Passes: followed by marks at least 40, in their original order.
hints: Selection changes membership without changing relative order.

practice.title: Compare sequence equality
practice.statementHtml: Read two counts (0..16), each followed by that many values (-99..99). Print Equal: 1 only when both order and values match.
hints: Equal membership is weaker than equal sequences.

quiz.prompt: Which description belongs to an ADT rather than its implementation?
options: Append a value and report whether it succeeded
Store values in adjacent int cells
Use a next pointer in each node
Double the reserved allocation
quiz.explanation: An ADT promises behavior. Cell layout and allocation policies describe implementations.

quiz.prompt: For repeated access by roll index, which representation fits directly?
options: Unindexed singly linked list
Array
Unordered chain of allocations
A cycle with no index
quiz.explanation: An array calculates an element location from its index. A chain must follow links.

quiz.prompt: Which relationship makes a tree non-linear?
options: Every node has exactly one successor
All values are integers
A node can have several children
The allocation never changes
quiz.explanation: Branching creates several possible paths; integer values and allocation policy do not determine shape.

quiz.prompt: What does static capacity mean for the marks bag example?
options: The marks cannot change
The count must always equal capacity
Every operation has constant time
The maximum number of stored marks is fixed
quiz.explanation: Fixed capacity limits size. You can still update values or hold fewer marks.

quiz.prompt: Why must an insertion interface report failure?
options: Storage limits or allocation failure can prevent insertion
Every insertion sorts the values
Integers are always immutable
An ADT cannot have edge cases
quiz.explanation: A caller needs to know whether the promised update happened, especially when capacity is exhausted.

quiz.prompt: A timetable lookup is rare but ordered printing is frequent. What should guide selection?
options: The longest structure name
The actual mix of required operations
Only the number of C keywords
The first representation encountered
quiz.explanation: Operation frequency and memory constraints matter together; one fast operation does not settle every choice.

quiz.prompt: Which pair can implement the same sequence ADT?
options: A compiler and a syntax error
A variable name and a comment
An array and a linked list
A printf format and an include guard
quiz.explanation: Both representations can support an ordered collection, even though their performance differs.

quiz.prompt: After updating one marks slot, which two marks remain at indices zero and one?
quiz.explanation: Only marks[1] changes to 91. marks[0] stays 72, so the line is 72 91.

quiz.prompt: How many live marks remain when the count begins below reserved capacity?
quiz.explanation: Size is three and the spare count is eight minus three, giving 3 5. Capacity does not count live marks.

quiz.prompt: Which mark does the first next link reach?
quiz.explanation: first.next identifies last, whose value is 85. The first node’s own 72 is not selected.

keyPoints.en: A data structure organizes values and the relationships between them.
keyPoints.bn: ডেটা স্ট্রাকচার মান আর তাদের মধ্যকার সম্পর্ক গুছিয়ে রাখে।

keyPoints.en: An ADT describes allowed operations without fixing the storage layout.
keyPoints.bn: ADT কী কী কাজ করা যাবে বলে; মেমরিতে কীভাবে থাকবে তা ঠিক করে না।

keyPoints.en: An array keeps its elements in adjacent memory locations.
A linked list stores sequence order through links between nodes.
keyPoints.bn: লিংকড লিস্টে নোডের লিংক ধরে ক্রম বোঝা যায়।

keyPoints.en: A structure choice depends on access, updates and memory limits.
keyPoints.bn: কীভাবে পড়বে, বদলাবে আর কত মেমরি আছে—এসব দেখে স্ট্রাকচার বেছে নাও।

examQuestions.question: Define an ADT and distinguish it from an array implementation.
examQuestions.answerHtml: An ADT specifies values and operations, such as inserting at a sequence position. An array implementation reserves adjacent cells and uses indices. The same ADT may use a linked representation.

examQuestions.question: Choose a representation for 60 fixed roll-number marks and justify two operations.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Use an array indexed by roll minus one. Reading or changing one mark takes O(1). Printing the class takes O(n). The fixed class size makes a capacity of 60 reasonable.

examQuestions.question: An array holds [72,85,91] with capacity five. Draw insertion of 64 at index one.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Before: [72][85][91][spare][spare]. Move 91 to index 3, then 85 to index 2. After: [72][64][85][91][spare]. Size changes from three to four; capacity stays five.
